the calculation of the weak form factors for the decays B → πlν, B → Klν, D → Klν and D → πlν in the framework of the Quark Conﬁnement Model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quark confinement approach, in spite of some approximations, is quite a successful one for the study of semileptonic decay form factors.
the QCDF model, in its present form, is not able to explain the large number of experimental data.
the QCD sum rule approach, which is based on the operator product expansion, is the most powerful tool for the calculation of the form factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the quark-confinement model can be a good candidate for a first principle approach to the heavy mesons.
we have found the form factors of the B and D meson decays to be consistent with the data, and we can explain the observed hierarchy of form factors.
the quark confinement potential is the most important ingredient in the description of hadron structure and hadron interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the form factors can be calculated in the QCM with a good accuracy without the need of fitting the model parameters.
the form factors of heavy mesons are determined by the quark mass, the confinement potential, and the quark propagator, which are all model-dependent.
the form factors of heavy-mesons decays can be calculated with a high accuracy without any free parameters.
